Hi Samantha and Tom,

Thanks again for the call today. Recap and recommended next steps below so we have a single thread for the compliance items you raised.

Call recap
- Primary need: process PHI for clinical summaries and scheduling, required HIPAA protections and a signed BAA.
- Secondary: SOC 2 Type II evidence for our hosted environment, and the ability to restrict logs and control retention.
- Performance: you expect steady throughput with occasional spikes tied to nightly batch imports.

Deployment options and fit for Elara Health
1) Hosted API (fastest to production)
   - Pros: quickest integration, low operational overhead.
   - Compliance: Redwood can operate under a signed BAA, we are SOC 2 Type II audited. We support KMS integrations, customer-configurable retention and PII scrubbing, and audit logs that can be restricted by role.
   - When to pick: good if you want fastest time-to-value and are comfortable with a BAA and controls around data access.

2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools)
   - Pros: predictable throughput and tenant isolation.
   - Compliance: same compliance controls as hosted plus stronger isolation guarantees in a dedicated pool. SLA options available.
   - When to pick: recommended if you need consistent latency and stricter tenancy isolation without full on-prem deployment.

3) Private VPC / On-prem (highest compliance)
   - Pros: customer-controlled networking, data never leaves your environment in on-prem installs.
   - Compliance: recommended when your audit requires full environment control, strict network segmentation, or additional third-party auditor requirements.
   - When to pick: enterprises with regulatory audits requiring on-prem evidence or customers who cannot accept any managed-host model. Typical lead time 8-12 weeks for on-prem.

Requested next steps
- Attached: Redwood SOC 2 evidence summary and a draft BAA for your legal team to review.
- Schedule a security deep-dive with Neha and a technical session with Dylan to go over network/firewall requirements and onboarding.
- If you prefer, we can start with Hosted + BAA and later move to Dedicated or Private deployment for full isolation.

Proposed meeting: Thu Apr 29 at 10:00am PT for security deep-dive. I copied Neha and Dylan to coordinate.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Samantha, thanks for the questions. Quick answers inline and notes for the Thu session.

1) Hosted logging and KMS
- We can disable payload logging for PHI by default and enable only under an audited support workflow.
- Retention windows: configurable per-tenant; common presets are 0 days (no logs), 30, 90, and 365. We can set a custom retention during onboarding.
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and other cloud KMS providers for encryption at rest. Keys remain in your KMS account; Redwood only stores encrypted ciphertext.

2) BAA and SOC2
- Redwood will sign a standard BAA. Draft attached for your legal team to review.
- Attached SOC2 summary includes scope notes for encryption, access control, monitoring, and change management. For deeper evidence we can share our SOC2 report and selected supporting artifacts under an NDA.

3) On-prem vs Dedicated TCO (ballpark)
- Dedicated: lower implementation time, roughly 2-4 weeks to provision, predictable monthly commit. Typical delta vs Hosted is a modest uplift for reserved capacity but less than full on-prem.
- On-prem: higher upfront engineering and integration effort, plus support for on-prem licensing. Ballpark delta vs Dedicated depends on infra choices but plan for a higher one-time setup cost and higher ongoing ops. We will share a short cost comparison in the deep-dive.

Pre-reads for Thu 10am PT
- Redwood SOC2 summary (attached)
- Draft BAA (attached)
- Security questionnaire link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-soc2-evidence
- Please send a network diagram and a short list of the data elements you consider PHI so Neha can tailor the call.

I've sent a calendar invite to the proposed slot. Looking forward to the call.
